source.author: verg
source.text: Sol, qui terrarum flammis opera omnia lustras, tuque harum interpres curarum et conscia Iuno, nocturnisque Hecate triviis ululata per urbes, et Dirae ultrices, et di morientis Elissae, accipite haec, meritumque malis advertite numen, et nostras audite preces.
source.text_original: 'Sol, qui terrarum flammis opera omnia lustras, / tuque harum interpres curarum et conscia Iuno, / nocturnisque Hecate triviis ululata per urbes, / et Dirae ultrices, et di morientis Elissae, / accipite haec, meritumque malis advertite numen, / et nostras audite preces.
source.text_english: Sun, who with your flames survey all the works of the earth, and you, Juno, interpreter and witness of these cares, and Hecate, howled at by night in the crossroads of cities, and avenging Dirae, and gods of dying Elissa, receive these offerings, and turn your deserved divine power against the guilty, and hear our prayers.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: sed patriae valuere preces auditaque magnis vota deis: video nostro tot in aequore reges teque ducem.
reuse.text_original: sed patriae valuere preces auditaque magnis / vota deis: video nostro tot in aequore reges / teque ducem.
reuse.text_english: But the prayers for his country prevailed, and vows were heard by the great gods: I see so many kings in our sea, and you as leader.
